$comment: GENERATED by packages/engine-core/scripts/p262-emit-ldt-labels.mjs — do not hand-edit the LDT numbers; re-run the script against an LDT checkout at a named commit. declaredDifferences[].reason IS hand-authored: the divergence test fails on a difference whose reason is null, so a regeneration forces each difference to be re-explained.
method: legacy-design-tools' own labelEdges (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/buildableEnvelope/edgeLabeling.ts) bundled with this repo's esbuild and run over this repo's fixture inputs (rings, situs strings and road centerlines from src/depth-warm/fixtures/p262Parcels.ts and p262CurvedFrontage.ts). polygon-clipping is aliased to scripts/p262-ldt-polygon-clipping-stub.mjs because LDT's geometry.ts imports it at module scope while labelEdges never calls it.

declaredDifferences.reason: P-262 logical-edge grouping (item 2): this parcel's far-end lot line is two chords (5.29 m + 11.50 m, 0.02 degree turn), so the engine gives BOTH the line's role (rear) while LDT labels chords one at a time and keeps this 5.29 m chord a plain side. At HEAD the engine agreed with LDT here and instead disagreed on four edges of this ring.

The engine has no second-frontage / corner-clip rule for a parcel touching a second named street (A-177 defers the street-name dictionary and the road-class rules), so this edge is a plain side; LDT's secondNamedStreetEdge resolves the corner and applies the corner-side setback. Pre-existing at HEAD, not a P-262 class.

P-262 curved frontage (item 6): the engine grows the front over the whole frontage run of the situs-named street (same street, each line's own nearest road, turns <= 45 degrees), while LDT keeps the front on the single nearest chord and calls the rest of the curve side. This is the one class with no counterpart in the other path — a fix owed to LDT, not an accepted divergence.

P-262 logical-edge grouping (item 2): the frontage's two chords (12.34 m + 11.89 m, 1.0 degree turn) are ONE lot line, so both take the front role; LDT labels the nearer chord front and the artifact chord side_corner. At HEAD the engine disagreed here too (side_corner), so this difference is the same artifact class seen from the fixed side.

PRE-EXISTING rear-pick difference, not a P-262 class: this lot's curved back line is three chords whose turns (16.6 and 27.8 degrees) keep them three lines in both paths, and the two rear rules land on different chords of it (LDT on the 3.57 m chord, 45.8 m off the street; the engine on the 10.36 m chord, 41.8 m). Measured identical before and after P-262 (HEAD labels recorded 2026-09-16), so it is disclosed here rather than claimed as agreement.
